about: Stages and timing for the revenue-drop playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Stages carry the product they need, so a run on Discovery only or Engagement only is offered the other product's stages as skips. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: explain
stages.do: Break the Discovery drop down and rank its causes; add each candidate cause as a finding, and note which suspects it already ruled out.

stages.name: engagement-explain
stages.do: Split the Engagement purchase revenue change into buyers, orders per buyer and order value, check the data first, and add the biggest drivers as findings.

stages.name: numbers
stages.do: When two numbers for the drop disagree (Discovery and Engagement, a report and the explainer, Bloomreach and the user's BI), find out why and which one to trust. Record not_needed without running when they agree.

stages.name: feeds
stages.do: Check the pixel, the catalog feeds, the index jobs and Engagement event mapping. Record ruled_out without running it when the explainers' data checks were clean.

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

stages.name: api
stages.do: Check whether search itself broke: request volumes and errors by type and day. Record ruled_out when the explainer's daily shape shows no outage.

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

stages.name: journeys
stages.do: Check whether a live Engagement flow stopped sending or broke. Record ruled_out when the drop is all in search or category browsing with no fall in returning buyers.

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

stages.name: funnel
stages.do: Find where Engagement shoppers now drop off between view, cart, checkout and purchase, and whether the recovery flows still run. Record ruled_out when the Engagement explainer puts the drop on order value alone.

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.
the Engagement purchase data is incomplete or double-counted, so funnel counts would mislead until it's fixed.

stages.name: change
stages.do: Measure the recent change the explainers suspect, a Discovery rule or test or an Engagement campaign or scenario launch: did it cause the drop?

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

stages.name: rollback
stages.do: Switch off (or end) the rule that made it worse, from a fresh read and its own plan, staging first, each batch after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (or neither ran): there is no incident to chase.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.
no rule is to blame.
the harmful change is an Engagement campaign or scenario: the user stops it in the Engagement UI, recorded as a change, and no Discovery rule is rolled back.

stages.name: recovery
stages.do: After the fix has had time, compare the Discovery days since the fix with the days of the drop: did revenue recover?

skip_when.reason: Discovery revenue didn't drop beyond normal variation (or wasn't explained), so there is no Discovery recovery to check.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

no rule was rolled back, no Engagement change was stopped, and the feeds, API, journeys and funnel checks found nothing to fix, so there is no fix to measure. If a fix landed elsewhere, set the recovery date with stage --not-before instead.

stages.name: engagement-recovery
stages.do: After the fix has had time, compare Engagement purchase revenue since the fix with the days of the drop: did buyers, orders and order value recover?

skip_when.reason: Engagement revenue didn't drop beyond normal variation (or wasn't explained), so there is no Engagement recovery to check.
the two numbers differ by definition, not because revenue fell: there is no incident to chase.

no rule was rolled back, no Engagement change was stopped, and the feeds, API, journeys and funnel checks found nothing to fix, so there is no fix to measure. If a fix landed elsewhere, set the recovery date with stage --not-before instead.

notes.recovery_check_days: Days after the rollback stage finishes before the recovery stages are due. A week gives a whole weekday cycle after the fix, and Discovery reporting runs about 2 days behind. When the fix was a feed, flow or campaign change outside this run, or the rollback was skipped, record the fix date plus this on each recovery stage with stage --not-before.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet: a recovery stage found too few days since the fix in the data. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on. The change stage's too_early_to_tell is a final outcome here, not a wait: in an incident the rollback decision can't wait for two weeks of data, so it rests on discovery-rule-cleanup's own impact check.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, which product it needs in a run on both (product: the Discovery path is explain, api, rollback and recovery; the Marketing path is engagement-explain, numbers, journeys, funnel and engagement-recovery; feeds and change serve both), what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes, or was skipped). Checks an explainer already ruled out record ruled_out, which says why they weren't run, and numbers records not_needed when no two numbers disagree. A skip_when entry with all lists conditions that must every one hold. The rest of the run is offered as a skip when neither explainer found a drop beyond normal variation (each within_normal, or skipped because the run lacks that product), or when the numbers stage finds the gap is a difference in definitions (definition_gap). The numbers stage itself is never skipped for within_normal: a user's number that says revenue fell against an explainer that says it didn't is exactly what it reconciles. Each recovery stage is offered as a skip when its own explainer found no drop, and when nothing was fixed: the rollback was skipped or kept, the change stage found no harmful Engagement change, and the feeds, API, journeys and funnel checks found nothing (each fine, ruled out or skipped).
